title: Immune Responses: Layers and Coordination
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
Human immunity begins before a microbe enters tissue. Skin, mucus, cilia, enzymes, and acidic environments reduce entry or remove potential threats. If those barriers are crossed, innate cells and proteins respond rapidly. They recognize broad patterns associated with microbes or damaged cells, promote inflammation, engulf material, and recruit other components. “Broad” does not mean blind; it means that recognition is organized around recurring molecular patterns rather than a separately learned receptor for every past exposure.

Innate and adaptive immunity are analytically distinct but operationally connected. Dendritic cells and other antigen-presenting cells process material and display fragments to lymphocytes. Signals from the surrounding tissue help determine whether and how T cells become activated. Helper T cells can support B-cell maturation and antibody production, while cytotoxic T cells can kill infected cells presenting relevant antigen. Antibodies do not simply “shoot” a pathogen. Depending on their class and context, they can block attachment, label targets, or help activate other immune mechanisms.

Adaptive responses generate specificity through diverse B- and T-cell receptors. Cells whose receptors fit a relevant antigen can proliferate and differentiate. Some become short-lived effectors; others contribute to longer-lived memory. On later exposure, memory populations may respond faster or more effectively, but protection varies with the pathogen, the antigen, time, host condition, and changes in the target. Immune memory is therefore a biological capacity, not an unconditional guarantee.

Vaccination uses this capacity by presenting an antigen, genetic instruction, or weakened or inactivated material in a controlled form. The aim is to prepare protective responses without requiring the full disease. Outcomes should be described at the right level: a vaccine may reduce infection, symptomatic illness, severe disease, or transmission, and these effects need not be equal. Precise language matters because exaggerated certainty can damage trust just as surely as denying well-supported protection.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Immunity is a single military chain in which every cell performs the same task.

options.label: B
options.text: Protection emerges from connected layers whose effects and limits must be described precisely.

options.label: C
options.text: Antibodies always destroy pathogens without help from other mechanisms.

options.label: D
options.text: Immune memory guarantees lifelong prevention of every infection.

questions.answer: 正解：B。障壁、自然免疫、獲得免疫、記憶、ワクチンという連結した層と条件付き効果を扱います。Aは分業、Cは抗体の協働、Dは記憶の限界を無視します。

questions.prompt: Which option correctly pairs three pre-entry defenses with two innate functions after entry?

options.label: A
options.text: Skin, mucus, and cilia; pattern recognition and inflammation

options.label: B
options.text: Memory B cells, cytotoxic T cells, and antibodies; skin formation and acidity

options.label: C
options.text: Redshift, calibration, and enzymes; antibody class switching and vaccination

options.label: D
options.text: Only learned receptors before entry; no rapid response after entry

questions.answer: 正解：A。侵入前には皮膚・粘液・線毛など、侵入後には反復分子パターン認識、炎症、貪食、動員などが働きます。B～Dは段階や機能を取り違えます。

questions.prompt: The phrase “operationally connected” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: separated in practice even when named together

options.label: B
options.text: interacting in the actual production of a response

options.label: C
options.text: identical in receptor structure and timing

options.label: D
options.text: connected only by a military metaphor

questions.answer: 正解：B。分類上は区別できても、実際の応答形成では相互作用するという意味です。Aは接続を否定し、Cは同一性を主張し、Dは比喩だけに縮めます。

questions.prompt: Why can antigen-presenting cells serve as a bridge between innate and adaptive immunity?

options.label: A
options.text: They process encountered material and present fragments with contextual signals that help activate antigen-specific lymphocytes.

options.label: B
options.text: They replace every B cell and T cell with an identical innate receptor.

options.label: C
options.text: They prevent all surrounding tissue signals from affecting T cells.

options.label: D
options.text: They create immune memory without encountering material or displaying antigen.

questions.answer: 正解：A。取り込んだ物質の断片と周囲の信号をT細胞へ伝え、自然免疫の認識を抗原特異的応答の開始へつなぎます。B～Dは提示と活性化の役割を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which three antibody functions are identified in the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Blocking attachment, labeling targets, and helping activate other immune mechanisms

options.label: B
options.text: Producing skin, moving cilia, and acidifying the stomach

options.label: C
options.text: Killing every pathogen alone, regardless of class or context

options.label: D
options.text: Presenting all antigens directly to every lymphocyte without other cells

questions.answer: 正解：A。抗体は付着阻害、標識、他の免疫機構の活性化支援を行い得ます。Bは障壁機能、Cは単独万能化、Dは抗原提示細胞の役割との混同です。

questions.prompt: Which statement about immune memory is best supported?

options.label: A
options.text: Memory makes later disease impossible.

options.label: B
options.text: Memory can improve later responses, but protection depends on several conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: Only antibodies contribute to memory.

options.label: D
options.text: A changed target must be recognized exactly as before.

questions.answer: 正解：B。再曝露時の応答を改善し得ますが、病原体、抗原、時間、宿主状態、標的変化に依存します。Aは保証へ強め、Cは細胞性記憶を消し、Dは標的変化を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why is one number insufficient to describe a vaccine's effects?

options.label: A
options.text: Effects on infection, symptoms, severe disease, and transmission can differ and can vary by population, time, and pathogen change.

options.label: B
options.text: Every vaccine affects all outcomes equally in every population forever.

options.label: C
options.text: Only transmission matters; severe disease and symptoms are irrelevant.

options.label: D
options.text: No vaccine outcome can be measured or compared.

questions.answer: 正解：A。感染、発症、重症化、伝播は別の結果で効果量や持続が異なり、集団・時期・病原体変化も条件になります。B～Dは結果の多層性や測定可能性を否定します。

questions.prompt: What does “Immune memory is a biological capacity, not an unconditional guarantee” mean?

options.label: A
options.text: Memory can enable a faster or stronger response under relevant conditions, but it does not promise the same protection regardless of circumstances.

options.label: B
options.text: Memory always prevents infection for life under every condition.

options.label: C
options.text: Memory has no biological effect on later exposure.

options.label: D
options.text: Host condition, time, and target change cannot affect protection.

questions.answer: 正解：A。capacityは一定条件で応答改善を可能にする仕組みで、guaranteeのように条件を問わず結果を約束しません。B～Dは条件依存性を否定します。

questions.prompt: Which explanation best communicates vaccine value without exaggeration or dismissal?

options.label: A
options.text: Define the outcome and population, report comparison group, observation period, benefits, adverse events, and uncertainty, and distinguish imperfect protection from no value.

options.label: B
options.text: Promise perfect lifelong protection against infection, illness, and transmission.

options.label: C
options.text: Claim that any protection below 100 percent is useless.

options.label: D
options.text: Avoid reporting uncertainty, adverse events, or the outcome being measured.

questions.answer: 正解：A。対象結果・集団、比較群、期間、便益、有害事象、不確実性を示し、完全でないことと無価値を区別します。Bは誇張、Cは過小評価、Dは信頼を損なう不透明さです。
